description: US military procurement contract types (Armed Services Procurement Act of 1947 & Renegotiation Act of 1951), GOCO plant catalog, and facility tier definitions (1945-1960).

CPFF.name: Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee
CPFF.description: Government reimburses 100% of allowable incurred direct and indirect costs up to the funding ceiling (125% of target cost) plus a fixed dollar fee negotiated at award (typically 7% of estimated cost; statutory ASPA 1947 cap is 15% for experimental R&D, 10% for production). Fee does not grow if costs overrun.

FPIF.name: Fixed-Price-Incentive-Firm
FPIF.description: Negotiated target cost, target profit (9%), share ratio (80% government / 20% contractor), and ceiling price (125% of target cost). Underruns increase contractor profit by 20% of savings; overruns reduce profit by 20% of excess cost up to ceiling price, beyond which contractor absorbs 100% of losses.

FFP.name: Firm-Fixed-Price
FFP.typical_phase: Mature Follow-On Production Lots / Spares / Export
FFP.description: Fixed unit delivery price regardless of actual contractor cost. Contractor retains 100% of learning/efficiency savings (subject to Renegotiation Act of 1951 excess-profit review above 12% ROS) and bears 100% of cost overruns.

LETTER.name: Undefinitized Letter Contract
LETTER.typical_phase: Korean War Emergency Surge / Urgent Prototype Start
LETTER.description: Urgent authorization to proceed immediately before full price definitization. Government advances up to 25% of estimated contract value over up to 6 months at 85% provisional cost reimbursement before converting into a definitized CPFF or FPIF contract.
